front: What CMP, JPE and JPN do
back: CMP compares ACC with a number or the contents of an address and sets a flag. JPE jumps if equal; JPN jumps if not equal. There is no greater-than jump.
IN puts the code of the key pressed in ACC; OUT displays the character whose code is in ACC.
After END, so that tables and variables are not executed as instructions.
One row per instruction executed, with columns for ACC, IX and every memory location that changes.
Characters are their codes: adding 1 to a code gives the next letter; the code of a lower-case letter is 32 more than the upper-case one.
